newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Coach warns Auckland against complacency.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Coach warns Auckland against complacency.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 27 - Auckland coach Graham Henry delivered a short, rip-snorting team talk last night, warning his team it would be at their own peril if they took Otago lightly in tomorrow's NPC first-division rugby match at Eden Park.
Henry told his team he expected Otago to be desperate and dangerous in seeking a victory that would keep alive their hopes of a semifinals berth, NZPA reports.
"We've had some great games over the years, we enjoy going down to Carisbrook and playing down there, we enjoy playing them here," Henry said afterwards.
"I thought they were very unlucky in the national championship final last year. They played that game with huge hearts and they'll play tomorrow's game the same way."
Otago, he said, would be driven by pride and the sheer need for championship points.

"They've got to play well; they've got to win to make the semifinals. They've come off a loss in a game they probably thought they were going to win (against Canterbury) and that will make them even more determined to play well.
"I think all teams worth their salt are going to rebound off a loss with a huge amount of determination and they will play well unless they are in disarray. Otago are not in disarray."
And after spending the week working with his backs following their poor showing against Wellington last week, Henry is hoping for better tomorrow.

"We've covered a lot of things, but the big thing is that they have to be more assertive and demand the ball from the forwards otherwise those old fellows in the forwards will keep the ball all day," he said.

"We've got some very mature and experienced players in the forward pack who have played a lot of international football but we don't have the same mix in the backline so it is important they don't get overawed by the demands of the forwards."
Auckland go into tomorrow's game without hooker Sean Fitzpatrick, who was ruled out yesterday because of a gash to the right knee suffered in the game against Wellington.

Auckland: Adrian Cashmore, Waisake Sotutu, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Ofisa Tonu'u, Zinzan Brooke (captain), Andrew Blowers, Richard Fromont, Robin Brooke, Dylan Mika, Olo Brown, John Akurangi, Craig Dowd. Reserves -
Craig McGrath, Matthew Webber, Leo Lafaialii, Kevin Nepia, Paul Thomson, James Kerr, Romi Ropati.
